description:
A generic Enum higher-order body reaches the backend referencing a value that
was never materialized: "backend value N is unbound" /
"native attempted to materialize absent value as runtime value".

## THE ORIGINAL REPRO NO LONGER REPRODUCES -- do not start from it

This was filed saying two call sites of the same generic Enum HOF with DIFFERENT
closures already breaks, and that fixing it unblocks `enum_predicate_search` on
all three paths. Both statements are false at main 417c5b0b5:

    fn main() do
      xs = [1, 2, 3, 4]
      dbg(Enum.find(xs, :none, fn (x) -> x > 2 end))
      dbg(Enum.find(xs, :none, fn (x) -> x > 9 end))
      dbg(Enum.find_value(xs, :none, fn (x) -> if x > 2, do: x, else: nil end))
    end
    interp / run / build  =>  3 :none 3     ALL CORRECT

`enum_predicate_search` is green on all three lanes, and a 32-distinct-lambda
`Enum.find` ladder compiles and runs correctly (45 executables, 0.95s) after
fz-6gb. The two-distinct-closure case is fixed; whatever survives needs a
narrower trigger.

## LIVE REPROS at main 417c5b0b5

Two things still fail with this ticket's exact signature, and both re-enable
with it:

1. `compiler2::drive_test::compiler2_jit_and_backend_interp_agree_on_reusable_cons_exit_counters`
   -- currently `#[ignore]`d naming this ticket. Fails with:

       native lowering invariant failed: backend value ValueId(0) in executable
       ExecutableKey { activation: ActivationKey { function: FunctionId(32),
       arrow: Ty(23) }, need: Value } must be bound before runtime use

2. The `enum_tier0` fixture (matrix, deferred on all three paths), as its SECOND
   blocker. With its one `Enum.reduce/2` over Map line skipped (fz-bfh.3, the
   first blocker) it prints eight further correct values and then dies with
   `backend value 0 is unbound`.

Start from (1): it is a lib test, it is deterministic, and its fixture is small.

## Likely locus, unchanged

Activation specialization keying / demand-derived value materialization when one
generic body is specialized at 2+ distinct closure surfaces, where a
per-specialization value is demanded by one path but not materialized for the
other. Same family as fz-xqw (SpecKey/BodyKey planner split).

Note that fz-6gb has since changed the keying substantially -- bodies that merely
transport a closure brand now treat it as freight and share a key, while bodies
that CONSUME callable identity keep precise keys. Re-read
`World::canonical_activation_key` and `erase_transported_closure_identities`
before assuming the old specialization picture.

## Checks

- `compiler2_jit_and_backend_interp_agree_on_reusable_cons_exit_counters` is
  re-enabled (no `#[ignore]`) and passes.
- `enum_tier0` gets past the unbound-value failure (it still needs fz-bfh.3 to
  come off deferral entirely).
- Full lib + matrix at baseline or better.
title: Generic Enum HOF leaves a backend value unbound (reusable-cons exit counters, enum_tier0)
